workbook:cma-final:p16:ch5:q9.stem_md:
(MINIMIZATION AND UNBALANCED PROBLEM):
Consider the following data for the transportation problem:

| Factory | Distribution |  |  | Supply to be exhausted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | **(1)** | **(2)** | **(3)** |  |
| A | 5 | 1 | 7 | **10** |
| B | 6 | 4 | 6 | **80** |
| C | 3 | 2 | 5 | **15** |
| **Demand** | **75** | **20** | **50** | **145** |
|  |  |  |  | 105 |

Since there is not enough supply, some of the demands at the three destinations may not be satisfied. For the unsatisfied demands, let the penalty costs be Rupees 1, 2 and 3 for destinations (1), (2) and (3) respectively. Find the optimum allocation that minimizes the transportation and penalty costs.
workbook:cma-final:p16:ch5:q9.explanation_md:
Since the $\text{Demand} \neq \text{Supplies}$, this problem is an unbalanced problem. Hence a dummy factory is added with cost equal to penalty for all distribution destinations and supplies equal to 40 units. Now, apply Vogel’s Approximation Method to the resultant balanced matrix for finding the basic feasible solution with matrix given below:

| Factory | Distribution |  |  | Supply to be exhausted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | **(1)** | **(2)** | **(3)** |  |
| A | 5 | 1 | 7 | **10** |
| B | 6 | 4 | 6 | **80** |
| C | 3 | 2 | 5 | **15** |
| Dummy Row | 1 | 2 | 3 | **40** |
| **Demand** | **75** | **20** | **50** | **145** |

The initial solution is obtained below by Vogel’s Approximation method:

| Factory | Distribution |  |  | Supply to be exhausted | Row Penalty |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | **(1)** | **(2)** | **(3)** |  |  |  |  |  |
| A | 5 | 10 1 | 7 | 10 0 | 4 |  |  |  |
| B | 20 6 | 10 4 | 50 6 | 80 30 20 0 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 6 |
| C | 15 3 | 2 | 5 | 15 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 3 |
| Dummy Row | 40 1 | 2 | 3 | 40 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Demand | 75 55 40 0 | 20 10 0 | 50 0 | 145 |  |  |  |  |
| Column Penalty | 2 | 1 | 2 |  |  |  |  |  |
|  | 2 | 0 | 2 |  |  |  |  |  |
|  | 2 | 0 |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  | 2 |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

$$\text{Total Minimum Cost of transportation and the penalty costs} = 10 \times 1 + 20 \times 6 + 10 \times 4 + 50 \times 6 + 15 \times 3 + 40 \times 1 = \text{₹ }555\text{/-}$$
